requirements.verifier_assertion: test_discriminant_known_fields — K.discriminant() equals the known field discriminant for Q(zeta_5)=125, Q(zeta_7)=-16807, Q(sqrt(5))=5, Q(sqrt(-3))=-3, Q(sqrt(7))=28, Dedekind's cubic (x^3+x^2-2x+8)=-503, and x^3+3x^2+5=-135.

test_integral_basis_is_genuine — K.integral_basis() returns a list of n field elements (n = degree of T), each convertible via K.to_sympy(...); the returned basis spans a Z-module whose discriminant matches the field discriminant, contains 1, and is closed under multiplication.

test_maximal_order_and_ideal_arithmetic + test_cyclotomic_prime_decomposition + test_fundamental_identity_quadratic — K.maximal_order() must support integer scalar multiplication (`7 * ZK` denotes 7 times the maximal order) and equality comparison between such principal ideals.

test_maximal_order_and_ideal_arithmetic + test_cyclotomic_prime_decomposition + test_fundamental_identity_quadratic — K.primes_above(p) returns prime ideal objects exposing attributes .e (ramification index) and .f (inertia degree); they support integer powers, products, and equality comparison so that Prod(P_i ** e_i) == p * ZK can be checked directly.

test_public_functions_and_exports — prime ideal objects provide P.valuation(I) with semantics identical to prime_valuation(I, P); in Q(zeta_5), at the unique prime above 5, P.valuation(5*ZK)=4 and P.valuation(3*ZK)=0.

test_maximal_order_and_ideal_arithmetic + test_public_functions_and_exports — Dedekind's cubic (x^3+x^2-2x+8) has discriminant -503; 2 splits completely into 3 distinct prime ideals with e=f=1; prime_decomp(2, T=...) on this polynomial returns a list of length 3.
test_cyclotomic_prime_decomposition — In Q(zeta_7), 7 is totally ramified: exactly one prime ideal P with e=6, f=1, and P**6 == 7*ZK.

test_cyclotomic_prime_decomposition + test_public_functions_and_exports — In Q(zeta_7), an odd prime p is unramified and its inertia degree equals the multiplicative order of p mod 7: p=11 gives 2 primes with f=3, p=13 gives 3 primes with f=2, p=29 splits completely into 6 primes with f=1; prime_decomp(11, T=cyclotomic_poly(7)) returns a list of length 2.
test_fundamental_identity_quadratic — In Q(sqrt(5)), 2 is inert: exactly one prime ideal with e=1, f=2. In Q(sqrt(7)), 2 ramifies: exactly one prime ideal with e=2, f=1, and its square equals 2*ZK.

test_fundamental_identity_quadratic + test_maximal_order_and_ideal_arithmetic + test_cyclotomic_prime_decomposition — Any decomposition of p in K satisfies the fundamental identity Sum(e_i * f_i) = n (degree of K).
test_public_functions_and_exports — round_two(T) on a monic, irreducible, univariate integer-coefficient polynomial returns (ZK, dK); for cyclotomic_poly(5), dK == 125.

test_public_functions_and_exports — prime_decomp(p, T=...) performs prime-ideal decomposition directly from the defining polynomial and returns a list of prime ideals; prime_decomp(2, T=Poly(x^3+x^2-2x+8)) has length 3; prime_decomp(11, T=Poly(cyclotomic_poly(7))) has length 2.
test_public_functions_and_exports — prime_valuation(I, P) returns a non-negative integer; in Q(zeta_5), at the unique prime above 5, v_P(25*ZK)=8, v_P(5*ZK)=4, v_P(3*ZK)=0.
